name: ffmpeg.wasm
role: FFmpeg compiled to WebAssembly for in-browser transcodes; slower, size-limited
summary: WebAssembly build of FFmpeg run in a web worker, with single-thread and multi-thread cores. Gives browser pages the familiar ffmpeg command line over an in-memory filesystem: transcode, trim, mux, extract frames. Distinguishing strength: full FFmpeg filter and codec coverage in the browser, at the cost of a multi-MB core, much slower speed than native, and COOP/COEP plus SharedArrayBuffer for multithreading.
use_when: In-browser tool needs an arbitrary FFmpeg command or codec that WebCodecs lacks
Over Mediabunny when you need filtergraphs or exotic containers, accepting the speed cost
avoid_when: Any native or CI delivery: ffmpeg-ffprobe is far faster
Plain remux, trim or transcode in a browser: Mediabunny is smaller and faster
Frame-accurate decode of large video in the page: WebCodecs directly
license: MIT wrapper; bundled FFmpeg core is LGPL or GPL depending on included libraries (x264 is GPL)
notes: 2026-10-26: bundled core is FFmpeg n5.1.4 per the docs, older than native FFmpeg 8.x; check the core's license flags before shipping.
2026-10-26: no release since 0.12.15 (2025-01-07), though the repo was pushed 2026-09-29.

assessment.rationale: Last release 2025-01-07 (about 21 months) but repo pushed 2026-09-29. Bundled core is FFmpeg 5.1.4. Only browser route to full FFmpeg; irrelevant to native delivery where ffmpeg-ffprobe wins.
